deals_cleared.merger_description: Retail Payment Solutions Pty Ltd (**RPS**), which is owned by Coles Group Limited (**Coles**), proposes to acquire the business assets of Paydock Ltd, Paydock Holdings Pty Limited and Paydock AUNZ Pty Limited (together, **Paydock**) (the **Acquisition**).

events.title: Coles - Paydock - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Retail Payment Solutions Pty Ltd (RPS), which is owned by Coles
Group Limited (Coles), proposes to acquire the business assets of
Paydock Ltd, Paydock Holdings Pty Limited and Paydock AUNZ Pty
Limited (together, Paydock) (Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Coles is an Australian public company (ASX: COL) that primarily
operates supermarkets and retail liquor stores trading under the
Liquorland banner.
RPS provides payment acquiring services to Coles and a limited
number of other Australian retailers through its own payment
infrastructure, which supports the routing, processing and
settlement of in-store and online card transactions.
Paydock is a software group based in both Australia and the United
Kingdom. Paydock provides a payment orchestration platform to
merchants and financial institutions, which integrates multiple online
payment methods and payment service providers.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
Paydock supplies payment orchestration services, which RPS uses
in its supply of payment processing services.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third partes.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• There are no material horizontal overlaps between RPS and
Paydock.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rivals’ access to payment orchestration
services given the presence of multiple alternative suppliers of
those services.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rivals’ access to distribution of their
payment orchestration services and/or payment processing
services given the presence of multiple alternative acquirers of
those services.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

determination_table_content.details:
EQT Fund Management S.à r.l. (EQT), through a wholly owned
special purpose vehicle Elevate BidCo GmbH (Elevate), applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of
the shares in Exolaunch GmbH (together with its subsidiaries,
Exolaunch), as described in the transaction documents provided as

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and

The acquirer, Elevate, is a special purpose vehicle established for
and in connection with the acquisition. Elevate is wholly owned by
EQT X, a private investment fund controlled by EQT, an alternative
investment fund manager.
The target, Exolaunch, is headquartered in Berlin, Germany, and
manufactures and supplies satellite deployment hardware,
facilitating the integration and aggregation of a wide range of
satellites with different launch vehicles, deploying payloads into their
target orbits. Exolaunch also provides related satellite launch
mission management and deployment services, providing end-to-end
launch services including mission design, satellite testing, launch
capacity procurement, integration of satellites to launch vehicles,
and deployment into orbit.
Exolaunch operates through wholly owned subsidiaries in the USA,
France and Japan.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. There is no horizontal or vertical overlap in
Australia between the acquirer (or its connected entities) and
Exolaunch in the supply of satellite deployment hardware, and
satellite launch mission management and deployment services.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.

(**Infoblox**), a company jointly owned by Warburg Pincus LLC (**Warburg Pincus**) and by funds managed and/or controlled by Vista Equity Partners Management, LLC (**Vista**), proposes to acquire 100% of the equity interests in Kentik Technologies, Inc. (**Kentik**).

events.title: Notification waiver determination published
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Infoblox Inc. (Infoblox) applied for a notification waiver in respect of
its proposed acquisition of 100% of the equity interests in Kentik
Technologies, Inc. (Kentik), as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
3 August 2026

The acquirer, Infoblox, is jointly owned by Warburg Pincus LLC
(Warburg Pincus) and by funds managed and/or controlled by Vista
Equity Partners Management, LLC (Vista).
Infoblox is a provider of IT automation and security services.
Infoblox offers core network management and security solutions for
Domain Name System (DNS), Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
(DHCP), and Internet Protocol (IP) address management across on-
premise, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments. It also offers asset
discovery, DNS-layer threat protection, security analytics, threat
intelligence, and related support, professional, education, and
managed services delivered directly and through partners. Infoblox
is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
The target, Kentik, is a US-based network observability and
intelligence software supplier, offering a cloud-based platform that
collects, analyses, and contextualises network telemetry data across
on-premise, hybrid, and cloud environments. Its network monitoring
tools help network administrators to keep track of the health and
performance of modern, complex networks. Kentik is headquartered
in San Francisco, California.
Vista also holds a controlling equity position in LogicMonitor, Inc.
(LogicMonitor), a SaaS-based performance monitoring platform for
hybrid IT infrastructures and cloud services, which supplies
observability software.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Infoblox and Kentik in
the supply of observability solutions and network
performance monitoring
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of core network management and
security solutions, and observability and network
performance monitoring solutions, post-acquisition
c. LogicMonitor and Kentik’s combined share in the supply of
observability and network performance monitoring solutions
in the Asia-Pacific region, and globally, is low and the
increase in share of supply arising from the Acquisition
would be small
d. there are alternative global suppliers of both core network
management and security solutions, and observability and
network performance monitoring solutions, in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

determination_table_content.details:
Salesforce, Inc. (Salesforce)’s proposed acquisition of 100% of the
shares in Contentful Global, Inc. (Contentful) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Salesforce, is a global supplier of customer
relationship management (CRM) software and other software-as-a-
service solutions. Salesforce’s modular CRM platform assists users
with sales, service, marketing and commerce functions.
The target, Contentful, is a global supplier of digital experience
software, specifically, a content management system. Contentful’s
content management system is used by businesses to create, edit,
organise and publish a company's digital content across various
channels and platforms via Application Programming Interfaces
(API). Contentful provides a 'headless' content management
product, meaning it stores and manages an organisation's content
separately from the system that displays the content to the end
user.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
The Parties overlap in the supply of content management system
software. Salesforce also offers products that can interoperate with
Contentful’s content management system.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and feedback from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• There is minimal horizontal overlap between Salesforce and
Contentful in the supply of content management systems.
Salesforce’s current content management software is not
offered as a standalone product and is limited in its capabilities
compared to those of Contentful as well as other content
management systems and digital experience platforms.
• Post-acquisition, the merged firm would continue to face
competition from alternative suppliers of content management
systems, including Acquia, Adobe, Contently, Optimizely and
Sanity.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival providers of content management
systems via an anti-competitive bundling or tying strategy given
there are alternative suppliers of CRM services in Australia and
internationally. Market feedback also indicates that the merged
firm would continue to have the incentive to maintain
interoperability between its software and rivals’ products.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

determination_table_content.details: | MicroStar Logistics – Kegstar (MN-30003) MicroStar Logistics – Konvoy MN-30003 This document contains a summary of the ACCC’s reasons for its determination of 7 August 2026. This document does not constitute the statement of the ACCC’s reasons for making the determination pursuant to sections 51ABZE(4)(b) and 51ABZZI(1)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth). The statement of the ACCC’s reasons will be published separately following a review for confidential information. Summary of Reasons 1. On 17 June 2025, Kegstar Pty Limited (Kegstar), sought informal clearance from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) to acquire certain Australian assets of Konvoy Holdings Pty Limited (Receivers and Managers Appointed) (Subject to Deed of Company Arrangement) (Konvoy) (together, the Parties). On 23 October 2025, the ACCC announced that it opposed the acquisition. 2. Following the ACCC’s opposition, the Parties elected to seek clearance for the acquisition under Australia's new merger regime. On 6 February 2026, Kegstar lodged a notification with the ACCC in respect of Kegstar’s proposed acquisition of certain Australian assets of Konvoy (the Acquisition). The effective notification date was 20 February 2026.1 3. On 1 April 2026, the ACCC decided the Acquisition would be subject to a Phase 2 review and subsequently issued a Notice of Competition Concerns to Kegstar on 13 May 2026.2 The ACCC published a summary of the Notice of Competition Concerns on the Acquisitions Register on 14 May 2026.3 4. The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition must not be put into effect. A summary of the ACCC’s reasons for its determination is set out below. 1 [Redacted - confidential]. 2 ACCC, Phase 2 Decision, 1 April 2026, 72969.001.016.0500; ACCC, Notice of Competition Concerns, 13 May 2026. 72969.001.075.0001. 3 ACCC, Notice of Competition Concerns – Summary, 13 May 2026. 72969.001.037.0269. 1

| MicroStar Logistics – Kegstar (MN-30003) Keg pooling in Australia 5. Brewers use keg pooling services to facilitate distribution of kegged alcoholic beverages to licensed venues without needing to own, maintain or recover their own keg fleet. In Australia, brewers acquire keg pooling services from one of two providers – Kegstar or Konvoy. In summary: ▪ Kegstar introduced keg pooling services into Australia in 2012, when it commenced its keg pooling business. ▪ Konvoy entered the market in 2019 and rapidly emerged as a direct competitor to Kegstar, with competition between the Parties manifesting through active rivalry for customers and improved pricing, service offerings and commercial terms. ▪ Following a period of successful operation, Konvoy sought to expand into the United Kingdom and made investments in the development of a keg tracking technology platform. It then started experiencing increasing financial difficulties from 2024. ▪ Konvoy unsuccessfully sought additional capital and its secured lender declined to provide further funding in 2025. In March 2025, Konvoy entered administration and the secured lender appointed Messrs Crawford and Smith of McGrathNicol as Receivers. ▪ The Receivers conducted a sale process across March and April 2025 in which [Redacted - confidential].4 ▪ The Parties entered into an Asset Sale Agreement on 20 June 2025,5 which, if completed, would result in Kegstar becoming the sole provider of keg pooling services in Australia. The ACCC’s statutory task 6. The ACCC recognises that participants in a receivers’ sale process may pursue different objectives. Receivers are required to maximise returns for creditors (and the company), and the purchase price is clearly a key factor in maximising those returns. However, execution risk is also a relevant consideration. Where a sale process results in a firm seeking to acquire its closest competitor – which can carry with it the highest purchase price – significant competition concerns are likely to arise. 7. The ACCC’s role is not to determine the most efficient ownership structure for an industry, nor is it to assist receivers in obtaining the highest return for creditors. Rather, as an administrative decision-maker under Part IVA of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act), the ACCC’s task is to assess the likely competitive effects of an acquisition in accordance with the statutory test. Under this regime, if the ACCC is satisfied that an acquisition, if put into effect, would, in all the circumstances, have the effect, or be likely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market, it may determine that the acquisition must not be put into effect. The ACCC’s assessment in this matter is directed to that statutory question. 4 [Redacted - confidential]. 5 [Redacted - confidential]. 2

| MicroStar Logistics – Kegstar (MN-30003) Competitive effects of the Acquisition 8. The ACCC has assessed the likely competitive effects of the Acquisition in the market for the supply of keg pooling services in Australia. While brewers have alternative methods of distributing beverages to licensed venues, including cans, bottles and self- supplied kegs, the ACCC considers that keg pooling services constitute a distinct and valued service offering, and therefore a relevant ‘market’. For many brewers, particularly small and medium-sized brewers seeking to distribute products beyond their local area, keg pooling avoids the capital investment, logistical and administrative costs, and risks associated with self-supply of kegs. 9. The ACCC has assessed the Acquisition and has made the following findings based on the evidence before it: ▪ Kegstar and Konvoy are each other’s closest competitor. The evidence before the ACCC indicates that Konvoy’s entry led to vigorous head-to-head competition between the Parties, which is still continuing, including substantial price reductions, improved commercial terms and active rivalry for customers. ▪ If the Acquisition proceeds, Konvoy would cease to operate as an independent competitive constraint and Kegstar would become the sole provider of keg pooling services in Australia. The Acquisition would remove the only significant source of direct rivalry in the market. The ACCC considers that the loss of this head-to-head competition would be likely to reduce competitive pressure on Kegstar in relation to price, service quality, and commercial offerings to brewers. ▪ Absent the Acquisition, there is a real prospect that either an alternative purchaser would acquire Konvoy’s business as a going concern through a rapid and targeted sale process, or that a substantial proportion of Konvoy’s assets would otherwise be realised and deployed in competing keg pooling operations. ▪ Self-supply (following the Acquisition) would be unlikely to be sufficient to replace the competitive constraint currently imposed by Konvoy. While some larger brewers self-supply kegs and others may have the ability to do so for limited volumes or local distribution, the ACCC considers that a substantial portion of customers would be unlikely to switch to self-supply due to the significant capital investment, operational capability and ongoing logistical management required. ▪ Timely and sufficient new entry is unlikely. Although kegs and other key inputs are generally available, a new entrant would need to establish the operational capability, reputation and customer base sufficient to compete effectively. Konvoy’s management possessed a strong reputation and operational capability when it entered in 2019. However in the ACCC's view, the current limited availability of contestable customer contracts, likely customer consolidation following the Acquisition, and the challenges of achieving scale make timely and effective new entry unlikely. 10. Having regard to the matters outlined above, the ACCC considers that competition in the future with the Acquisition would likely be substantially less than in the future without the Acquisition. 11. The ACCC does not consider that the Proposed Undertaking offered by Kegstar addresses the extent of the competitive harm arising from the Acquisition. That harm is substantial and arises from a significant structural change in the market to a monopoly provider of keg pooling services in Australia. The ACCC considers that a behavioural and 3

| MicroStar Logistics – Kegstar (MN-30003) time-limited remedy would not sufficiently replicate the structural competitive constraint provided by an independent competitor. 12. For these reasons, the ACCC is satisfied that the Acquisition, if put into effect, would, in all the circumstances, be likely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the Australian keg pooling services market and has determined that the Acquisition must not be put into effect. 4
